title: Fabricated scientists and studies. Court imposes Estonia's first AI fine for AI hallucinations

reading.body:
This is a fabrication failure at the point where a party prepares a legal filing. The model produced citations to researchers and studies that do not exist, and those citations were carried into documents submitted to a court. The falsehood was not in the legal argument but in the supporting apparatus that gives an argument its authority.

The failure surfaced only when the court checked the references and found no such Estonian researchers and no such studies. Nothing in the preparation process caught it first. Catching it would have required verifying each cited source against a real record before filing, which is the same check the court ultimately performed.

The court treated the responsibility as belonging to the parties, not the tool, and fined them accordingly. What is not established is how the AI system was used, what it was asked, or whether anyone reviewed its output before submission.

reports.title: Fabricated scientists and studies. Court imposes Estonia's first AI fine for AI hallucinations

summary:
A Tallinn court fined ten plaintiffs after they submitted legal filings containing false academic references generated by artificial intelligence. The plaintiffs were challenging a logging permit and cited studies on clearcutting, but the court found the Estonian researchers did not exist and the studies could not be found. One plaintiff was fined 150 euros and nine others 50 euros each. The court said AI use is allowed, but parties remain responsible for the accuracy of their claims.

The court noted this is Estonia's first known case of fines over AI-generated content in a filing. Court chair Kaupo Kruusvee said AI use in court documents is growing and can slow proceedings because each submission still needs full review. He said courts do not use AI to draft decisions and warned that AI can produce fake references.
